items.stem: On a work package the planned value is 100, the earned value is 80 and the actual cost is 90 (all in thousands). What does this indicate?

options.text: The package is behind schedule and over budget
options.rationale: Correct: earned value below planned value means behind schedule, and earned value below actual cost means over budget.

options.text: The package is ahead of schedule and under budget
options.rationale: Ahead/under would require earned value above planned value and above actual cost.

options.text: The package is exactly on plan
options.rationale: On plan would require earned value to equal both planned value and actual cost.

options.text: The package is ahead of schedule but over budget
options.rationale: Earned value is below planned value, so it is behind schedule, not ahead.

items.explanation: Correct: earned value below planned value means behind schedule, and earned value below actual cost means over budget.

items.stem: Which TWO earned-value formulas are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Schedule variance = earned value minus planned value
Cost performance index = earned value divided by actual cost
Cost variance = actual cost minus earned value
options.rationale: Cost variance is EV - AC, not AC - EV.

options.text: Schedule performance index = planned value divided by earned value
options.rationale: SPI is EV / PV, not PV / EV.

items.explanation: Correct: SV = EV - PV and CPI = EV / AC are the standard definitions.

items.stem: A project reports a cost performance index of 1.1. What does this mean?

options.text: The project is earning more value than it is spending, so it is under budget
options.rationale: Correct: CPI above 1 means earned value exceeds actual cost.
CPI above 1 indicates under budget, not over.
CPI is a cost measure; schedule is read from SPI.

options.text: The project has overspent its contingency
options.rationale: CPI does not describe contingency usage directly.

items.explanation: Correct: a cost performance index above 1 means earned value exceeds actual cost, so the work is under budget.
